# Oriveo Community Edition

> Oriveo Community Edition is an open-source, bring-your-own-key (BYOK) multi-model AI chat client
> for iOS, Android and the web — a local-first, self-hostable alternative to a hosted ChatGPT or
> Claude plan, with no account and no subscription. It is an LLM client for fifteen model providers
> (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, DeepSeek and more) and for any OpenAI-, Anthropic-
> or Gemini-compatible endpoint, including Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp and vLLM on your own machine.

The three clients are native and separate: SwiftUI on iOS, Jetpack Compose on Android, Next.js on
the web, with a native macOS client in development. They share one definition of how to talk to a
provider — request recipes, capability contracts and recorded upstream byte streams — and all three
assert against the same fixtures. You pay each provider its own list price directly; Oriveo is the
client, not a reseller, and no server of ours sits in the chat path. Conversations, notes, folders,
skills and attachments stay on the device. Official builds of the commercial edition are at
https://oriveoai.com; this repository is the AGPL-3.0-or-later source you build yourself.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/oriveo/oriveo/blob/main/README.md): what Oriveo is, why it exists, the feature list, the provider table, the architecture, how to build each client, and the FAQ
- [iOS client](https://github.com/oriveo/oriveo/blob/main/ios/README.md): SwiftUI with a UIKit transcript and GRDB storage; iOS 18 and later; building it on your own iPhone
- [Android client](https://github.com/oriveo/oriveo/blob/main/android/README.md): Jetpack Compose with Room, Koin and Ktor/OkHttp; Android 8 and later; building the APK
- [Web client](https://github.com/oriveo/oriveo/blob/main/web/README.md): Next.js App Router with React, Zustand and TypeScript; Node 22; how to self-host it
- [macOS client](https://github.com/oriveo/oriveo/blob/main/macos/README.md): a native client in development, arriving in the coming months
- [Shared contracts](https://github.com/oriveo/oriveo/blob/main/shared/README.md): capability recipes, model contracts, recorded provider fixtures, and the OriveoProviderKit Swift package
- [Contributing](https://github.com/oriveo/oriveo/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): toolchain versions, how to build and test each client, and what a good pull request looks like
- [Scope](https://github.com/oriveo/oriveo/blob/main/COMMUNITY.md): what this edition is for, and the kinds of change it will not accept
- [Security policy](https://github.com/oriveo/oriveo/blob/main/SECURITY.md): how to report a vulnerability privately, and what counts as one in a bring-your-own-key client

## Facts

- Fifteen built-in providers, each reached with a key you create yourself: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Grok, Mistral, Groq, Together AI, Fireworks AI, MiniMax, Z.ai, Qwen, Kimi (Moonshot), SiliconFlow.
- Relay connections reach any OpenAI-, Anthropic- or Gemini-compatible endpoint, plus llama.cpp's native API, including one on your own LAN.
- Local model servers supported through Relay: llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, Open WebUI. iOS and Android discover them by mDNS where the engine advertises itself, else by probing the usual ports.
- OpenAI and Grok can also be used by signing in with a ChatGPT or Grok subscription you already hold, over each provider's own device-authorization flow, instead of an API key.
- No account and no analytics. Nothing to sign in to; the iOS and Android clients contain no reporting SDK, and the web bundle's Sentry stays silent without a DSN of your own.
- Two read-only requests of Oriveo's own: a public model catalog, read in two calls — one for how each model wants to be addressed, one for the facts about individual models. Neither carries a key, a conversation, or an identifier attached by Oriveo.
- Self-hosting: the web client (`NEXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL`) and the Android build (`-PORIVEO_METADATA_BASE_URL`) can be pointed at a catalog host of your own; on iOS that override is a Debug-build convenience only.
- On iOS and Android chat requests go straight from the device to the provider. On the web most pass through the Next.js route handler serving the app — your own machine when you run it locally — because most provider APIs send no CORS headers.
- Storage: iOS Keychain for provider keys, Android `EncryptedSharedPreferences` under an Android Keystore key, and, on the web, unencrypted IndexedDB — a browser offers no equivalent facility, so iOS or Android gives the stronger guarantee. Conversations, notes, folders, skills and attachments live on the device, exportable to a file.
- Sixteen interface languages, including a full right-to-left layout for Arabic.
- Licensed AGPL-3.0-or-later. Community Edition builds use the `ai.oriveo.community` identifier prefix and can sit alongside a store build.
- There are no prebuilt binaries in this repository; Community Edition is source you build yourself.
